overall.line: A wine bar requires Conditional Use Authorization and a Type 42 license transferred from another bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District; live music needs a Place of Entertainment permit; both paths face discretionary hearings whose outcomes the records do not settle.

findings.text: Planning Code § 762 designates bar use as conditional (C) on the first story in the NCT-VALENCIA district; hours between 6 a.m. and 2 a.m. are principally permitted, and 2 a.m. to 6 a.m. require conditional use.

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District (§ 249.60) permits a restaurant operating as a bona fide eating place to serve alcohol, but a new or relocated bar is conditional use only and must use a license transferred from another bar within the SUD.
An active Type 41 On-Sale Beer & Wine Eating Place license is on file at 995 Valencia St (Sarita's Grill & Beer), issued November 3, 2023.

Transitioning from a Type 41 restaurant license to a Type 42 bar license constitutes a change of use under Planning Code § 102, because Type 42 permits bar operation without the food-service requirement that defines a Type 41 eating place.
findings.verification_note: The record discusses SUD rules but does not mention § 102, Type 41/42 licenses, or that transitioning between them constitutes a change of use.

findings.text: Within 1,000 ft, only 3 dated use decisions for bars or restaurants appear in the last 10 years: 1 approved (2011 Type 41 to Type 47 upgrade at this building), 2 withdrawn (a bar-within-restaurant at 970–974 Valencia in 2010, a restaurant with Type 41 at 1021 Valencia in 2019); N = 3 is too small to establish an approval rate.
findings.verification_note: The 1021 Valencia record describes a mixed-use development with restaurant infrastructure, not specifically a restaurant with Type 41 license.

findings.text: The only CUA for a new bar use within 1,000 ft in NCT-VALENCIA zoning was withdrawn before hearing in January 2011 (970–974 Valencia, filed August 2010).

zoning.name: Valencia Street Neighborhood Commercial Transit District
zoning.rules: Bar requires Conditional Use Authorization; Restaurant principally permitted (First Story). Bar C on the First Story only; Liquor Store NP; within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD (§ 249.60), a new Bar must use a license transferred from another Bar in the SUD.

overlays.name: Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District
overlays.effect: No new Liquor Stores. A Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place may serve alcohol (licenses may be transferred in from inside or outside the SUD), as may non-profit theaters, bowling alleys/mini-golf with an integrated Restaurant, single-screen movie theaters (beer and wine) and ABC Type 90 music venues. A new or relocated Bar is considered under the underlying zoning but only as a Conditional Use, and must use a liquor license transferred from another Bar within the SUD. Existing liquor establishments may relocate or expand only with CU. East of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street, any new Restaurant requires CU and new ABC Type 75 (brewpub) licenses are prohibited. Good-neighbor operating conditions (§ 202.2 plus lighting and window-signage limits) apply.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar-within-restaurant proposal at 970-974 Valencia (66 m away), same NCT-VALENCIA zoning and Mission Alcohol SUD constraints that this wine bar faces. Filed 2010, withdrawn January 2011.

The record does not state why the applicant withdrew, but withdrawal signals the difficulty of winning approval for new bar uses in this Special Use District.

This wine bar closes at 1 a.m., well within the principally permitted 6 a.m.–2 a.m. window, so the POE approval path is established.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Active POE at Arcana, 2512 Mission (150 m, NCT-MISSION)—restaurant with nighttime entertainment, approved for live performance in a similar mixed restaurant-and-entertainment model.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Arcana's POE approval for a restaurant-plus-entertainment concept 150 m away demonstrates that the Entertainment Commission supports food-and-music venues on the Mission corridor. The wine bar's small-plates kitchen and occasional live music fits this restaurant-entertainment hybrid model.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Planning approved a POE referral for 998 Valencia (52 m, NCT-VALENCIA) in 2014 as accessory to retail use, capping entertainment at one-third of floor area—an agency referral showing Planning's standard for entertainment-as-accessory in NCT-VALENCIA.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning's 2014 referral response for 998 Valencia approved entertainment as accessory to the primary retail use, limited to one-third of gross floor area per Planning Code 703.2 and Police Code 1060(r). An agency referral, so it reflects Planning's permitting posture rather than a Commission decision, but it confirms that entertainment is allowed accessory to a principal use in NCT-VALENCIA.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Withdrawn CUA at 2519 Mission (210 m, NCT-MISSION) for a 5,958 sq ft restaurant with Type 41 license and live entertainment, filed July 2019, withdrawn October 2019—another withdrawn entertainment-and-alcohol case nearby.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A restaurant-plus-live-entertainment CUA at 2519 Mission was withdrawn three months after filing. A use decision case that was withdrawn; the record does not state why. Two withdrawals (this and 2010.0680C) among the few bar/entertainment CUAs within 1,000 ft suggest applicants face hurdles, though neither record explains the cause.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Planning approved continuation of an existing Type 41 license at 1007 Valencia (45 m, NCT-VALENCIA) in 2008, explicitly noting it does not establish a new bar use—an agency referral showing Planning's distinction between continuing and creating bar uses.

An agency referral that flags the Mission Alcohol SUD's scrutiny: even renewing an existing license, Planning clarified it was not authorizing a new bar, underscoring that new bar uses require CUA and transferred Type 42 licenses within the SUD.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Planning approved Entertainment Commission POE referral for Arcana at 2512 Mission (152 m, NCT-MISSION) in November 2020 for restaurant and nighttime entertainment—agency referral matching this wine bar's restaurant-plus-entertainment profile.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning recommended approval of Arcana's POE for restaurant and nighttime entertainment uses in NCT-MISSION in 2020. An agency referral (not a Commission hearing), so it shows Planning's staff posture: food-primary venues with entertainment are permitted. The wine bar's limited kitchen and live music fit this model.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Approved CUA at 2410-2412 Mission (193 m, NCT-MISSION) in July 2007 to change from bar use to retail—demonstrates Planning approved eliminating a bar use, though it does not test approval of a new bar.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved converting an existing bar to retail at 2410 Mission in 2007. A use decision that removed a bar use rather than creating one, so it does not predict approval of a new bar, but it confirms that bar uses existed historically in NCT-MISSION and required CUA to change.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Approved CUA at 2526-2548 Mission (159 m, NCT-MISSION) in December 1999 for outdoor activity area with full-service restaurant/bar—shows Commission approved bar use paired with restaurant and outdoor seating on Mission corridor.

A use decision from 1999, so predates the Mission Alcohol SUD restrictions, but it shows the Commission historically permitted bar uses on the Mission corridor when tied to full-service restaurants.

filing_playbook.action: Form LLC with California Secretary of State and obtain EIN from IRS
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization online ($70) and apply for an EIN the same day (free, immediate). Use the LLC name on the lease, bank account, and all permit applications. File the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20).

filing_playbook.action: Register business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector and file Fictitious Business Name statement
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online to receive a Business Account Number (BAN), which every other city department requires. File the FBN statement with the County Clerk and publish in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks. Budget $55–95 registration fee (tiered by projected gross receipts) plus $60–120 for the FBN and publication.
filing_playbook.verification_note: The record shows registration fee range is $55-700, not $55-95.

filing_playbook.action: Pre-application meeting with Planning to confirm Type 42 license transfer requirement and CUA timeline
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Ask Planning staff: (1) Is a Type 42 license available for transfer from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD? (2) Does the existing Type 41 at this address simplify the CUA or set any precedent? (3) Will the limited kitchen qualify as bona fide food service to support a restaurant-with-bar classification? Bring a floor plan, menu outline, and the lease. Request a written answer on the license-transfer requirement before filing the CUA.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Records confirm Type 42 transfer requirement and CUA process but do not mention an existing Type 41 license at 995 Valencia St.

filing_playbook.action: File Conditional Use Authorization application for bar use under § 762 and § 249.60
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Frame the concept as a wine bar with limited food service (small plates available during all hours of alcohol service) to align with the restaurant-with-bar model permitted under the Mission Alcohol SUD. Emphasize closing at 1 a.m. (within principally permitted hours), limited capacity (40 seats), and good-neighbor commitments (security plan, noise monitoring, litter control). Reference nearby POE approvals (Amados, Arcana) to show compatibility with the corridor. Submit the $3,100+ CUA fee (2026–27 rate) and budget 6–10 months for pre-application community meeting, environmental review, Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Records don't specify principally permitted hours, don't mention Amados/Arcana approvals, and don't confirm the fee as the 2026–27 rate.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain California Seller's Permit (CDTFA) and begin ABC Type 42 license application or transfer
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online for the seller's permit (free, often same-day). If a Type 42 license is available for transfer from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD, engage an ABC license broker to escrow and transfer it; budget 90–180 days and confirm the CUA is approved or close to approval before paying the deposit. If no transferable license exists, confirm with Planning that a new Type 42 application will satisfy § 249.60 before proceeding. Submit the ABC application with the signed lease, zoning sign-off (pending CUA approval), and post the 30-day public notice at the premises. Expect ABC to flag undue concentration (9 on-sale licenses within 500 ft) and require a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from Planning or the Board of Supervisors, adding 1–3 months.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Records show 60-150 days (not 90-180), and do not detail ABC application requirements, CUA timing advice, or PCN delay estimate.

filing_playbook.action: Entertainment Commission intake meeting for Place of Entertainment permit
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email the Deputy Director to confirm zoning eligibility (CUA pending or approved) and schedule an intake meeting. Present the concept as a wine bar with occasional live music (e.g., Thursday–Saturday until 1 a.m.) as an accessory use, not a primary nightclub model. Bring a floor plan showing the performance area (≤200 sq ft for accessory entertainment per Planning Code 703.2), a sound plan (acoustic treatment, monitoring protocol), and the good-neighbor policy. Reference nearby POE approvals (Amados at 998 Valencia, Arcana at 2512 Mission). Submit the $2,708 application fee (2026–27) and post a 30-day notice; budget 45–120 days to hearing.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Records do not mention Planning Code 703.2 or the 200 sq ft performance area limit for accessory entertainment.

filing_playbook.action: Hire architect, submit DPH plan check and building permit application
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Engage an architect experienced in SF restaurant build-outs. Submit DPH plan check ($828–1,241 for limited cooking in 2026–27) with two sets of scaled drawings, equipment layout, finishes, menu, and hand-sink locations. Route the building permit through DBI with Planning (construction review), Fire (hood suppression, egress), Public Health, and PUC (FOG). Budget 2–4 months for plan review. Schedule a pre-final DPH inspection at ~80% construction and a final inspection at least two weeks before opening. Install the grease interceptor before DBI final sign-off and submit the FOG Installation Verification Form to SFPUC for the sewer-bill reduction.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Records give fees by project type, not cooking type; don't specify two sets or hand-sinks; say book inspections two weeks ahead, not before opening; imply but don't state interceptor timing.

filing_playbook.action: Final inspections, certifications, and ancillary permits before opening
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Ensure one owner/employee holds a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate and all food employees obtain Food Handler Cards. Register for Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) training ($3 portal + $10–25 course per person) for all alcohol servers and managers. Set up workers' comp insurance (quote through a broker or State Fund) and register as an employer with EDD. Subscribe to organics hauler service (SB 1383). Apply for ASCAP and BMI public-performance music licenses ($300–2,500 each, formula-based). Schedule Fire Department hood and egress inspection if required. Complete DPH final inspection ($470 Permit to Operate application in 2026–27) and receive the health permit before serving food. File for sign permit if installing exterior signage ($300–1,500).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Records do not mention Food Handler Cards, organics hauler/SB 1383, BMI licenses, or Fire Department hood/egress inspections.

timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization for bar use + Type 42 license (transfer or new application with PCN finding) + Place of Entertainment permit, in parallel with building permit and health permit
timeline_cost.notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per catalog entry, realistically 6–10 months including pre-application meeting, community outreach, environmental review, Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period). The CUA application fee is $3,100+ (2026–27 rate for no construction; higher if tenant improvements exceed thresholds). In parallel, the ABC Type 42 license will take 60–150 days if a transfer from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD is available, or 90–240 days if ABC flags undue concentration and the City must issue a Public Convenience or Necessity finding (likely, given 9 on-sale licenses within 500 ft). If no transferable Type 42 exists within the SUD, the bar use cannot proceed under current zoning unless Planning issues a written exemption. The Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, $2,708 application fee in 2026–27) can be filed after the CUA is approved or in late stages; Entertainment Commission will want zoning confirmation. Building permit plan review (2–4 months, $800–15,000 depending on scope) and DPH plan check + health permit (21–60 days plan check, 14–45 days final permit; $828–2,500 plan check, $470 permit application in 2026–27) run in parallel with the CUA. Total government fees (excluding ABC license purchase if transferring): CUA $3,100, POE $2,708, DPH plan check + health permit $1,298–2,970, building permit $800–15,000, business registration $55–700, other state/federal $0 (EIN, seller's permit, RBS, workers' comp quotes vary), sign permit $300–1,500 = approximately $8,300–$26,000. Timeline is 7–15 months from CUA filing to opening, with the CUA hearing as the long pole; if the CUA is denied or the Type 42 transfer requirement cannot be met, the concept cannot open as a bar. The two withdrawn bar CUAs within 1,000 ft (2010.0680C, 2017-013728CUA) signal approval risk, though the records do not state why applicants withdrew. Budget contingency time and legal/consultant fees for the CUA and ABC undue-concentration response.
timeline_cost.verification_note: Catalog shows ABC Type 42 as 60-150 days only; extended timeline with PCN, Planning exemption process, and several fee items in the total are not stated in the cited records.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits in the NCT-VALENCIA district where bars require Conditional Use Authorization and face the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District's strict rule: a new or relocated bar must use a Type 42 license transferred from another bar within the SUD. The address has operated as a restaurant (Sarita's Grill & Beer) with an active Type 41 license since 2023; the building spans 991–999 Valencia and has hosted full-service restaurants for over two decades. Within 500 ft sit 9 active on-sale ABC licenses (51 within 1,000 ft) and 24 registered food/drink businesses—high density that triggers ABC's undue-concentration review and a likely Public Convenience or Necessity finding requirement. Only 3 dated use decisions appear in the last 10 years within 1,000 ft (1 approved, 2 withdrawn), too few to establish an approval rate, though nearby entertainment permits (POE at 998 Valencia, Extended Hours at 2500 Mission) show the Entertainment Commission does grant late-night approvals on this corridor.
data_gaps: No hearing transcripts or detailed conditions available for the two withdrawn bar CUAs (2010.0680C, 2017-013728CUA) to understand why applicants withdrew.
No detail on whether the existing Type 41 at 995 Valencia restricts bar-style operation or has good-neighbor conditions.
The base-rate sample is too small (N=3 in 10 years) to predict Planning Commission approval likelihood for a new bar CUA.
No record of whether any Type 42 licenses are available for transfer within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD.
Sound-study or acoustic-mitigation requirements for POE permits on this block are not documented in the application records.
